Taj Mahal Practical Visitor Guide 2026

Everything you need to know before visiting the World Wonder in Agra: official Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) ticket fees, strict Friday rules, East vs West gates, security scans, and avoiding high-commission emporiums.

1 Strict Friday Closure Rule

The Taj Mahal is strictly closed to general tourists every Friday. It only opens briefly for local residents to attend Friday afternoon congregational prayers (Jummah) at the Taj Mosque.

⚠️ Critical Itinerary Note: If your trip to Agra falls on a Friday, do not panic! Agra Fort, Fatehpur Sikri, Itimad-ud-Daulah (Baby Taj), and Mehtab Bagh remain 100% open on Fridays. You can enjoy a full day of sightseeing at these world-class monuments and visit the Taj Mahal on Saturday morning at dawn.

2 Official 2026 Ticket Rates & Online Booking

The Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) has instituted cashless, mandatory advance online ticketing. The ticket includes monument grounds entry, with an optional separate ticket required to climb the marble plinth into the main mausoleum chamber.

Visitor Category Grounds Entry Main Dome Plinth Total Official Cost
Foreign Tourists (Non-Indian) ₹1,100 ($13 USD) ₹200 ($2.50 USD) ₹1,300 ($16 USD)
SAARC & BIMSTEC Nations ₹540 ₹200 ₹740
Indian Citizens ₹50 ₹200 ₹250
Children (Under 15 Years) FREE FREE FREE
💡 Booking Pro-Tip: Foreign tourist tickets include a 500ml sealed bottle of drinking water and shoe covers (necessary for walking on the white marble plinth). When you book any private tour through TajMahal.City, our local concierge procures your fast-track ASI QR e-tickets in advance, bypassing all ticket window queues.

3 Best Entry Gate: East Gate vs West Gate

The Taj Mahal complex has three historic gates, of which two are currently active for general public entry:

East Gate (Recommended for Sunrise)

Closest to the Fatehabad Road luxury hotel zone (Oberoi Amarvilas, ITC Mughal, Taj Hotel & Convention Centre). Far less congested with heavy domestic tour buses early in the morning. Electric eco-golf carts shuttle guests from the parking area (approx 1 km) directly to the gate barrier.

West Gate (Main City Gate)

Handles the majority of large domestic coach tours and day-trippers coming directly from Agra Cantt Railway Station. While closer to central Agra markets, queues at the West Gate ticket counter and CISF security lines can be significantly longer during peak midday hours.

*Note: The South Gate (historic Darwaza-i-Sirhi) is primarily used for exit and remains closed for general entry.

4 Prohibited Items & CISF Security Protocols

Security at the Taj Mahal is handled by the Central Industrial Security Force (CISF). Stringent airport-style metal detectors and body scans operate at both gates. Separate queues exist for men and women.

🚫 Strictly Forbidden Items Inside Monument:
  • Tripods, monopods, and camera gimbals/stabilizers (handheld smartphones & DSLRs are permitted).
  • Drones and aerial video gear.
  • Power banks, external chargers, and long cables.
  • Lighters, matchboxes, tobacco, cigarettes, e-cigarettes, and alcohol.
  • Food items, candy, chewing gum, and open drinks (unopened water bottles are allowed).
  • Knives, scissors, and sharp metallic objects.

Lockers & Cloakrooms: Secure government cloakrooms operate near the ticket counters at both East and West gates. However, leaving items in luggage lockers adds 15–20 minutes of queue time. We strongly advise leaving all prohibited electronics and heavy backpacks inside your private air-conditioned tour car with your chauffeur.

5 Avoiding Common Agra Tourist Scams

Agra is one of the world's most famous travel destinations, and unwary visitors often encounter high-pressure tourist traps. Here is how to protect yourself:

  • 1. The "Free / Cheap Guide" Trap: Touts outside Agra Cantt or near parking lots offering guide services for ₹100–₹200 are not certified historians. Their primary goal is to guide you quickly through the monument and then steer you to commission-paying marble emporiums or jewelry shops where prices are inflated by 300%.
  • 2. The Forced Shopping Detour: Standard tour bus packages frequently build "mandatory artisan factory visits" into the itinerary. At TajMahal.City, we maintain a strict 100% No Forced Shopping Guarantee — your time is reserved solely for heritage.
  • 3. The "Gate is Closed" Misdirection: Auto-rickshaw drivers may tell you the East Gate is closed due to a VIP visit or construction, offering to take you to a "special handicraft emporium" instead. Never believe this without checking with official police booths.

Frequently Asked Questions

What are the best sunrise hours to visit the Taj Mahal? +
The monument gates open 30 minutes before official sunrise (approx 05:30 AM in summer and 06:15 AM in winter). Arriving at the gate 20 minutes before opening guarantees you are among the first 20 people inside, allowing for iconic crowd-free photography of the reflective pools and central marble plinth.
Can I visit both the Taj Mahal and Agra Fort in one morning? +
Yes. A classic morning circuit begins with the Taj Mahal at dawn (05:45 AM – 08:30 AM), followed by a leisurely breakfast, and then a 2-hour exploration of Agra Fort (94-acre red sandstone citadel just 2.5 km away) before midday heat sets in.
Is there a dress code for entering the Taj Mahal? +
While there is no strict religious dress code for the outer gardens, the Taj Mahal is an active Islamic mausoleum. Modest clothing covering shoulders and knees is recommended out of cultural respect. Inside the main domed chamber housing the cenotaphs, shoes must be covered with disposable covers (provided with foreign tickets) or removed. Silence must be observed inside the mausoleum.
How far is Agra from Delhi, and what is the best travel method? +
Agra is 210 km (130 miles) southeast of Delhi. The two most comfortable travel modes are: (1) A private chauffeured AC car via the 6-lane Yamuna Expressway (approx 3 to 3.5 hours door-to-door), or (2) The Gatimaan Express high-speed train from Hazrat Nizamuddin Station (Delhi) to Agra Cantt (1 hour 40 minutes).
